claim: The latest Mantine release on npm as of 2026-07-14 is @mantine/core 9.4.1, published 2026-06-28.
Mantine 9.0.0 shipped on March 31, 2026; it is a feature/theming release (defaultRadius sm->md, fontWeights theme key) with no rework of the CSS-modules/PostCSS styling architecture.

The 8.x->9.x migration guide lists no breaking changes to the PostCSS preset or cascade layers; the styling breaking change is that `light` variant CSS variables became solid colors instead of transparent.
quote: In Mantine 9, the `light` variant CSS variables were changed to use solid color values instead of transparency.

claim: Every Mantine package that ships CSS also ships a parallel `styles.layer.css` in which all rules are wrapped in `@layer mantine`, making Mantine overridable regardless of import order.
quote: All `@mantine/*` packages that export styles have an additional file in which all styles are wrapped in the `@layer mantine` directive. ... CSS rules within a layer are grouped together and applied before rules without a layer.

claim: `@mantine/core/styles.css` includes a minimal CSS reset (body margin 0, box-sizing border-box, font inheritance on form elements) plus :root/body styles and static utility classes, so it collides with Tailwind Preflight.
quote: The `@mantine/core` package includes minimal CSS reset – it includes only basic styles required for components to work in modern browsers.

claim: postcss-preset-mantine supplies the light-dark(), rem()/em() functions and @mixin hover / smaller-than / larger-than mixins used in Mantine CSS modules, and is explicitly optional, not required.
quote: It is not required to use it, but is highly recommended.

claim: postcss-preset-mantine is at 1.18.0, last published 2025-06-30 - it is stable/low-churn and shared across Mantine 7/8/9.
Mantine has no dedicated 'Usage with Tailwind' docs page; the official FAQ answer is to disable Tailwind preflight, otherwise follow a community GitHub discussion.
quote: Usually it is enough to disable preflight to prevent global styles from affecting Mantine components.

claim: In Tailwind v4 all utilities live inside cascade layers, so unlayered Mantine `styles.css` rules beat Tailwind utilities - the exact regression vs v3 that users hit with Mantine.
quote: This is caused by the fact that Tailwind utility classes are now in cascade layers, which have lower precedence than rules not in any layer. You can remove them from the cascade layer like so: @layer theme, base, components, utilities; @import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme); @import "tailwindcss/preflight.css" layer(base); @import "tailwindcss/utilities.css";

claim: The canonical Mantine+Tailwind4 discussion (opened 2025-02-06): the v3 recipe (corePlugins.preflight:false + @layer tailwind) is dead; top-voted fix is declaring `@layer theme, base, mantine, components, utilities;` then importing tailwindcss and `@mantine/core/styles.layer.css`.
A user reports Mantine's postcss.config.cjs (postcss-preset-mantine + postcss-simple-vars) coexisting with Vite's Lightning-CSS-based @tailwindcss/vite plugin with no PostCSS conflict.
quote: Hello , I've used it with 'postCss' and worked well ... module.exports = { plugins: { 'postcss-preset-mantine': {}, 'postcss-simple-vars': {...} } } ... @import "tailwindcss"; @import "@mantine/core/styles.css"; ... Note: I'm using Vite with the `@tailwindcss/vite` plugin

claim: Tailwind v4 removed `corePlugins.preflight:false`; disabling the reset now means importing theme.css and utilities.css individually and omitting preflight.css.

tailwind-preset-mantine (176 stars, last push 2026-06-23) is a third-party Tailwind v4 preset that fixes layer order (theme -> base -> mantine -> components -> utilities) and maps Mantine theme tokens into Tailwind.
tailwind-preset-mantine 4.1.0 was published 2026-06-23, i.e. the community bridge is actively maintained in 2026, but it is a single-maintainer package.
A working Next.js + Mantine + Tailwind v4 setup runs both PostCSS plugins in one postcss.config.mjs and uses the mantine cascade layer plus useComputedColorScheme for SSR-safe dark mode.
Mantine theming is pure CSS custom properties (--mantine-color-{name}-{0..9}) generated by MantineProvider, with a cssVariablesResolver hook - so Tailwind can consume Mantine tokens via var().
quote: Each color defined in `theme.colors` object is required to have 10 shades. Theme color can be referenced by its name and shade index, for example, `--mantine-color-red-6`.

claim: Mantine's Styles API exposes a classNames prop targeting every inner element of a component, which is the seam through which Tailwind utility classes are injected.
quote: The Styles API is a set of props and techniques that allows you to customize the style of any element inside a Mantine component – inline or using the theme object.
